maneuvers.label: Inspect the back and spinal alignment

normalFinding.default: Spine straight with normal curvature; shoulders and iliac crests level.

steps: Look at the standing patient's back from behind and the side.
Check posture and spinal curves.
Compare heights of the front and back pelvic landmarks on both sides.

normalFinding.default: No spinous process or paraspinal tenderness.

steps: Press on each spinous process from the neck down to the sacrum.
Then feel the muscles on either side of the spine.
Ask about tenderness.

normalFinding.default: Full painless spinal flexion, extension, lateral bending and rotation.

steps: Ask the standing patient to bend forward and then lean back.
Ask them to bend to each side.
Ask them to twist the trunk to each side.

normalFinding.default: Straight leg raise negative bilaterally; no radicular pain reproduced.

steps: Have the patient lie flat on the back.
Keeping the knee straight, slowly lift one leg by the heel.
Ask if pain shoots down the leg; repeat on the other side.

normalFinding.default: FABER negative bilaterally; no hip or sacroiliac pain.

steps: With the patient supine, place one ankle on the opposite knee in a figure-four.
Steady the opposite side of the pelvis with one hand.
Gently press the bent knee toward the table and ask about pain; repeat on the other side.

normalFinding.default: Shoulders symmetric without deformity, swelling, wasting or discoloration.

steps: Expose both shoulders.
Compare from the front and back for symmetry and muscle bulk.

normalFinding.default: No tenderness over the bony landmarks, AC joint, bicipital groove or rotator cuff muscles.

steps: Feel the scapular spine, acromion and acromioclavicular joint.
Feel the biceps tendon in its groove at the front of the shoulder.
Feel the trapezius, deltoid and rotator cuff muscle bellies.

normalFinding.default: Full painless shoulder flexion, extension, abduction, internal and external rotation bilaterally.

steps: Ask the patient to raise both arms forward, then reach back.
Ask them to raise the arms out to the sides overhead.
Check internal rotation (hand up the back) and external rotation (hands behind the head).

normalFinding.default: Hawkins test negative bilaterally.

steps: Raise the patient's arm forward to shoulder height with the elbow bent to 90 degrees.
Steady the shoulder and rotate the forearm downward to turn the shoulder inward.
Ask about pain; repeat on the other side.

normalFinding.default: Neer test negative bilaterally.

steps: Steady the scapula with one hand.
With the arm straight and thumb down, lift it forward overhead as far as it will go.
Ask about pain; repeat on the other side.

normalFinding.default: Empty can test negative; supraspinatus strength 5/5 without pain bilaterally.

steps: Have the patient hold the straight arms out at 90 degrees, angled slightly forward, thumbs down.
Press down on the forearms while they resist.
Note weakness or pain on either side.

normalFinding.default: External rotation strength 5/5 without pain bilaterally.

steps: Ask the patient to keep the elbows tucked at the sides, bent to 90 degrees.
Ask them to rotate the forearms outward against your hands.
Compare strength and pain on both sides.

normalFinding.default: Elbows symmetric without swelling, deformity or discoloration.

steps: Expose both elbows.
Compare carrying angle, contour and skin on each side.

normalFinding.default: No tenderness over the medial or lateral epicondyles or olecranon.

steps: Feel the lateral epicondyle and the medial epicondyle.
Feel the olecranon at the back of the elbow.
Ask about tenderness and note swelling.

normalFinding.default: Full painless elbow flexion, extension, pronation and supination bilaterally.

steps: Ask the patient to bend and straighten both elbows.
With elbows at 90 degrees at the sides, turn the palms down and then up.

normalFinding.default: Hands and wrists symmetric without swelling, deformity, wasting or discoloration.

steps: Look at the backs and palms of both hands.
Check the joints for swelling or deformity.
Compare the thenar and hypothenar muscle bulk.

normalFinding.default: No tenderness, warmth or swelling of the wrist, CMC, MCP, PIP or DIP joints.

steps: Feel across the wrist joint.
Squeeze gently over the thumb base, knuckles and each finger joint.
Note tenderness, warmth or bogginess.

maneuvers.label: Wrist and hand range of motion

normalFinding.default: Full painless wrist and finger range of motion bilaterally; full fist.

steps: Ask the patient to bend the wrists up and down, then tilt them side to side.
Ask them to straighten the fingers fully.
Ask them to make a tight fist with both hands.

maneuvers.label: Rise from chair without using arms

normalFinding.default: Rises from the chair easily without using the arms.

steps: Ask the seated patient to fold the arms across the chest.
Ask them to stand up from the chair.
Watch for effort, use of the arms or rocking.

normalFinding.default: Hips, knees, ankles and feet symmetric without deformity, swelling or discoloration.

steps: Ask the patient to stand with legs exposed.
Compare the hips, knees, ankles and feet from front, side and back.

normalFinding.default: No tenderness over the iliac crests or greater trochanters.

steps: Feel along each iliac crest.
Feel over the greater trochanter on the side of each hip.
Ask about tenderness.

normalFinding.default: Full painless hip extension bilaterally.

steps: Have the patient lie face down or stand.
Move the straight leg backward from the hip.
Note range and pain; repeat on the other side.

normalFinding.default: Full painless hip flexion bilaterally.

steps: With the patient lying on the back, bend the knee.
Bring the knee up toward the chest.
Note range and pain; repeat on the other side.

normalFinding.default: Full painless hip internal and external rotation bilaterally.

steps: With the patient supine, flex the hip and knee to about 90 degrees.
Swing the foot outward to rotate the hip inward, then inward to rotate it outward.
Note range and pain; repeat on the other side.

normalFinding.default: Full painless hip abduction and adduction bilaterally.

steps: With the patient supine, steady the pelvis.
Move the straight leg out to the side, then back across the midline.
Repeat on the other side.

normalFinding.default: Knees symmetric without swelling, effusion, deformity or discoloration.

steps: Expose both knees with the patient lying flat.
Compare contour, alignment and skin on each side.

normalFinding.default: No joint line, patellar, fibular head or popliteal tenderness; no effusion.

steps: Feel the medial and lateral joint lines with the knee slightly bent.
Feel the patella and the fibular head.
Feel the back of the knee for swelling.

normalFinding.default: Full painless knee flexion and extension bilaterally.

steps: Ask the patient to bend each knee as far as possible.
Then ask them to straighten it fully.

normalFinding.default: Collateral ligaments stable to varus and valgus stress bilaterally.

steps: Bend the knee to about 30 degrees with the patient lying flat.
Hold the thigh steady and push the lower leg inward then outward.
Feel for gapping at the joint line; repeat on the other knee.

normalFinding.default: Anterior and posterior drawer tests negative with firm endpoints bilaterally.

steps: Bend the knee to 90 degrees with the foot flat and steady it by sitting lightly on it.
Grip the top of the shin and pull it forward.
Then push it backward; note excess movement and repeat on the other knee.

normalFinding.default: Ankles and feet symmetric without swelling, deformity or discoloration.

steps: Look at both ankles and feet from all sides, including the soles.
Compare for swelling, colour change or deformity.

normalFinding.default: No tenderness over the malleoli, Achilles tendon, navicular or base of the fifth metatarsal.

steps: Feel the inner and outer ankle bones.
Feel along the Achilles tendon.
Feel the navicular and the base of the fifth metatarsal.

normalFinding.default: Full painless dorsiflexion, plantarflexion, inversion and eversion bilaterally.

steps: Ask the patient to pull the foot up and point it down.
Ask them to turn the sole inward and then outward.
Compare sides.
